metadata.title: SanDisk slides over 14% as bearish NAND pricing outlook hits chip stocks

content.text:
SanDisk (Nasdaq: SNDK) shares fell over 14% to $80.68 in Friday noon trading, losing $13.72, as a bearish outlook for NAND flash memory prices in 2027 raised concerns about the company's earnings prospects.
The decline followed a report from memory-market research firm TrendForce forecasting that NAND contract prices could remain flat or fall by as much as 5% quarter on quarter in the first quarter of 2027, before declines spread across all product categories from the second quarter.
TrendForce also cut its forecast for fourth-quarter 2026 NAND contract price increases to 8%–13%, from an earlier estimate of 15%–20%, while noting that spot prices had already fallen more than 20% as distributors cleared inventory.
The outlook is a particular concern for SanDisk because its business is entirely focused on NAND flash, leaving it more exposed to a downturn in memory pricing than diversified chipmakers such as Micron.
SanDisk has committed approximately half of its fiscal 2027 NAND bit supply and two-thirds of its fiscal 2028 supply through long-term agreements with hyperscale customers, although investors remain concerned about whether these contracts can protect margins if prices weaken.
Thursday's reported 87.4% plunge in SanDisk shares was a technical adjustment caused by its eight-for-one forward stock split, rather than an actual collapse.
SanDisk Corp shares appeared to plunge 87.4% on some trading screens on Thursday, alarming investors, although the actual decline during the session was over 18%.
The misleading figure resulted from the company's eight-for-one forward stock split, which took effect at 4.01pm Eastern time on Thursday. The adjustment divided the price of each existing share by eight, creating an apparent fall of 87.5% when some data feeds compared the new split-adjusted price with the previous, unadjusted close.
The broader technology sector also weakened, with the Nasdaq falling 2.1% and the S&P 500 declining 0.9%. Micron, Western Digital, Seagate, AMD and TSMC also fell sharply, reflecting wider pressure on semiconductor valuations.
